title: Choose the darker visual world
question: This round abandons polished-editorial defaulting. Which darker system feels unmistakably yours?

options.label: Indoor Weather
options.lineage: monofrequency light installations and mirrored halls
options.thesis: One artificial sun reveals the different lives and bodies of work gathered beneath it.
options.viewport: A vast dark hall crosses the fold; four silhouettes and their reflections anchor service, software, research, and study.
options.case: It is atmospheric without becoming cyberpunk, though the person can recede behind the spectacle.
options.risk: The light installation may become more memorable than the work.

options.label: Load Paths
options.lineage: tensegrity sculpture and structural force diagrams
options.thesis: Military leadership, software, research, and study hold one another in useful tension.
options.viewport: A tall responsive force structure replaces the hero grid; following a cord reveals the evidence it connects.
options.case: The systems metaphor fits the subject and creates a distinctive interaction without borrowing a military interface.
options.risk: The structural metaphor needs disciplined copy to remain immediately legible.

options.label: Night Reference
options.lineage: reference-setting pages and mechanical ruling engines
options.thesis: A narrow living index keys a candid record while the wide black margin keeps it severe and quiet.
options.viewport: Two short columns sit small inside a dark field, split by one movable red key rail and surrounded by working notes.
options.case: It is the clearest written portrait in the hand, but still carries an editorial distance.
options.risk: Dense reading may slow a recruiter’s first scan.

options.label: Midnight Riso
options.lineage: two-ink small-press zines and deliberate misregistration
options.thesis: Two offset voices—disciplined and curious—overlap into the person behind the résumé.
options.viewport: A split-ink opening statement shifts against a blunt project index; overlap becomes the active state.
options.case: It is personal and memorable, but louder than the quiet-confidence brief.
options.risk: Print energy can make serious experience feel like a side project.

options.label: Night Cross-Check
options.lineage: a small aircraft’s night instrument six-pack
options.thesis: Six calm instruments each hold one truth; together they describe the person you can trust in the dark.
options.viewport: A disciplined six-part constellation cross-checks identity, service, software, research, study, and selected work.
options.case: It wins on recognition and product clarity, provided the page uses instrument logic without cockpit cosplay.
options.risk: Handled literally, it reduces a full person to an Air Force theme.

options.label: Ink Current
options.lineage: suminagashi marbling and live fluid systems
options.thesis: The site’s dark surface remembers where service, code, research, and curiosity have moved through it.
options.viewport: A still margin holds the facts while one responsive ink current carries the eye through the work.
options.case: It feels alive and singular, but the interactive material explains less on first contact.
options.risk: The fluid effect can become expensive decoration.

canonCard.label: Conventional portfolio
canonCard.thesis: A polished hero, project grid, résumé timeline, and contact block executed cleanly.
canonCard.viewport: Name and title above a familiar project-card grid.
canonCard.risk: Easy to understand, easy to forget.
